diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the global bilinear form $\bilB$ is coercive (e.g., when $\divergence \velField \equiv 0$), \cref{th:msgfem:global} below always holds.

issues.failure_explanation: Global coercivity does not imply the displayed coercivity inequality on an oversampling domain. For divergence-free velocity, integration by parts in the locally defined form produces an uncontrolled artificial-boundary term, namely minus one half of the integral of $(\velField\cdot\bn)v^2$ over the interior part of the subdomain boundary. The local error has no boundary condition there that makes this term nonnegative or zero. The subsequent local continuity estimate in the diffusion seminorm also invokes a local Poincare-type control that is not established for unrestricted restrictions of the global solution. Consequently, the claimed bound by $(1+C\peclet_H)^2$ is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a valid stability estimate for every local solution operator that handles artificial-boundary fluxes and proves the required uniform energy bound, possibly with different constants, and then redo the contraction argument. Alternatively, weaken the corollary and iteration theorem to assumptions under which such local stability is explicitly guaranteed.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit divergence-free global estimate in the corollary is unproved. The iteration theorem's proof invokes that estimate to obtain a uniform contraction, so its convergence conclusion is also not established by the given argument.
issues.title: Local coercivity is incorrectly inferred from global coercivity
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a nontrivial local stability argument or a meaningful weakening of the hypotheses and constants, but it need not replace the overall MS-GFEM architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The corrections produced by the local and coarse spaces lie in the homogeneous Dirichlet test space, so they do not change an incompatible Dirichlet trace of the initial guess. An arbitrary element of $H^1(\Omega)$ can have a nonzero, nonconstant trace on $\Gamma_D$; such an iterate cannot converge in the diffusion energy to the solution in the homogeneous Dirichlet space. Moreover, the MS-GFEM approximation estimate used for $I-G$ applies when the exact solution associated with the right-hand side is the input function, which requires that input to belong to the test space.

failure_location.quote: the sequence of MS-GFEM iterates $\{\fwp^{(k)}\}_{k=0}^\infty$ defined by \cref{eq:msgfem:iteration} converges for any initial guess $\fwp^{(0)} \in \Hone$ strictly monotonically:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require $\fwp^{(0)}\in\fwpTestSpace$, or at least require it to have the same Dirichlet trace as $\fwpSol$, and formulate the operator estimate only on the resulting homogeneous error space.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's contraction guarantee is false for the stated class of initial guesses, independently of the separate gap in its stability proof.
issues.title: Iteration cannot converge from an arbitrary H1 initial guess
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis on the initial guess completely resolves this defect without changing the method, rate, or relevant iterative guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Let $Q=\sum_j R_j^T\chi_j B_j^{-1}R_j$ and $C=R_S^TB_S^{-1}R_S$. The two-stage residual update gives the preconditioner $Q+C(I-BQ)$, because the residual after the fine correction is $(I-BQ)r$. The displayed formula instead gives $Q+C(I-Q)$ and therefore neither represents the stated MS-GFEM map nor agrees with the subsequently displayed RAS steps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final factor by $I-\discBilForm\sum_j\discRestriction^T\discPU\discBilForm_j^{-1}\discRestriction$, making the matrix formula agree with the two-stage residual update.
issues.overall_effect: The paper gives two incompatible definitions of the discrete preconditioner; implementing the first displayed matrix literally does not implement the claimed hybrid RAS procedure.
issues.title: Displayed preconditioner omits the stiffness matrix in the multiplicative coarse correction
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and routine, and the correctly stated two-stage procedure already identifies the intended algorithm without requiring a new construction or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Lastly, we define the positive part $(\velField\cdot\bn)^{\oplus} := \max(\velField\cdot\bn, 0)$ and negative part $(\velField\cdot\bn)^{\ominus} := \max(-\velField\cdot\bn, 0)$ of the normal flow.

issues.failure_explanation: For the conservative flux $-A\nabla u+\velField u$, an inflow face has $(\velField\cdot\bn)u=-(\velField\cdot\bn)^-g$. Moving this known flux to the right-hand side contributes $+(\velField\cdot\bn)^-gv$. Expanding the quoted outer minus instead contributes $-(\velField\cdot\bn)^-gv$, imposing the opposite convective inflow data. The diffusion Nitsche terms in the same bracket have the standard signs, so the defect is specifically the convection term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the sign of the $(\velField\cdot\bn)^-v$ term inside the bracket, equivalently write its right-hand-side contribution with a positive sign, and verify the affected boundary-driven numerical runs against the corrected formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The DG scheme as written is inconsistent with the stated Dirichlet boundary condition on inflow boundaries. This affects the checkerboard and transport experiments, whose nonzero data are prescribed on an inflow edge.
issues.title: DG inflow Dirichlet contribution has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: The mathematical discretization is repaired by one forced local sign correction; the operator and preconditioning architecture are otherwise unchanged.
